sections.label: Tightened travel agent licence criteria
sections.summary: The criteria travel agents must fulfil to be granted a licence have been tightened.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: First, we have tightened the criteria that travel agents must fulfil in order to be granted a licence.

sections.label: Reduced show cause period
sections.summary: The show cause period for a travel agent facing potential suspension and revocation was reduced from 21 to 14 days.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Third, we have reduced the "show cause period" for a travel agent facing potential suspension and revocation, from 21 to 14 days.

sections.label: Higher penalty for unlicensed agents
sections.summary: Clause 5 raises the penalty ceiling for unlicensed travel agent activities from $10,000 to $25,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Clause 5 raises the penalty ceiling for the offence of unlicensed travel agent activities from $10,000 to $25,000.

sections.label: Administrative financial penalties introduced
sections.summary: Clause 7 introduces administrative financial penalties set at a maximum of $2,000 for minor contraventions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Clause 7 introduces administrative financial penalties set at a maximum of $2,000 for minor contraventions.

sections.label: Disclosure of suspension or revocation
sections.summary: Clause 7 allows STB to require travel agents to disclose to all customers that they have been issued a notice of suspension or revocation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Clause 7 allows STB to require travel agents to disclose to all customers that they have been issued a notice of suspension or revocation.

sections.label: Niche licence tier for local tours
sections.summary: A niche licence tier is intended in the Travel Agents Regulations for travel agents selling or arranging local tours with passenger-carrying conveyance but without accommodation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: For instance, we intend to introduce a "niche licence" tier in the Travel Agents Regulations targeted at travel agents who sell or arrange local tours with passenger-carrying conveyance, but without accommodation.

sections.label: Niche licensee capital requirements
sections.summary: Niche licensees would need $50,000 in paid-up capital and net worth, versus $100,000 for general licensees.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: At the moment, we intend to require niche licensees to meet a minimum requirement of $50,000 in paid-up capital and net worth, compared to $100,000 for general licensees.

sections.label: Phased implementation from 2018
sections.summary: MTI and STB will work towards implementing these changes in phases from 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: MTI and STB will work towards implementing these changes in phases from 2018.

sections.label: Travel agent licence changes
sections.summary: The changes tighten licensing criteria, enhance STB investigation powers, shorten the show cause period to 14 days, and adjust penalties.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: First, to tighten the criteria that travel agents must fulfil in order to be granted a licence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Second, to enhance STB's investigation powers when dealing with errant travel agents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Third, to reduce the "show cause period" for travel agents facing licence suspension or revocation from 21 days to 14 days and allow STB the option to require such travel agents to disclose this fact to their customers during this period.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Fourth, to adjust the penalty framework to introduce administrative financial penalties for more minor contraventions, allowing STB to take more timely action against such contraventions, while raising the maximum fines to curb more serious contraventions.

sections.label: Travel agency closure complaints
sections.summary: CASE received 792 complaints over five years about travel agency closures, mostly for lost deposits, with 17 agencies ceasing operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Over the past five years, CASE has received 792 complaints against the closure of travel agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Most of these complaints relate to loss of deposits paid by consumers due to the closure of travel agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: And based on our records, there were a total of 17 travel agencies which ceased operations over the last five years.

sections.label: Consumer confidence and travel fairs
sections.summary: Consumer confidence in travel agencies will be lost, and media reported travel fair sales of about $80 million to $100 million yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: There will also be loss of consumer confidence in travel agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: It has been reported in the media that the amount of sales generated by travel fairs every year has been about between $80 million and $100 million.

sections.label: Insurance or performance bond level
sections.summary: Insurance or performance bond may be set at 20% to 30% of each travel agent's annual turnover so funds are not tied up excessively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The amount of insurance or performance bond may be set at 20% to 30% of the annual turnover of each travel agent so that their funds are not tied up excessively.

sections.label: CASE supports Travel Agents Act amendments
sections.summary: CASE supports the amendments to the Travel Agents Act and enhanced consumer protection measures, and urges STB to regularly review legislation and regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In summary, CASE supports the amendments to the Travel Agents Act and the introduction of enhanced measures to protect consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: We urge STB to regularly review the legislation and the regulations to ensure that consumer interests will always be protected.

sections.label: Sudden closures of travel companies
sections.summary: The sudden closure of companies including Five Stars Tours and MISA Travel left many consumers in the lurch.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Yet, the sudden closure of companies, including established players, such as Five Stars Tours and MISA Travel, left many consumers in the lurch.

sections.label: Revoked licences and ceased operations
sections.summary: The website lists two companies with revoked licences and 125 companies that ceased operations since 1 January 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: On the website, there are two companies which had their licences revoked and 125 companies that had ceased operations since 1 January 2017.

sections.label: Net worth capital for restricted licences
sections.summary: The proposed amendments require restricted travel agents to have a net worth capital of $50,000, and asks whether a percentage could be ring-fenced to pay workers and guides.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Under the proposed amendments for restricted travel agents' licence, there is a requirement of a net worth capital of $50,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Can we ring-fence a percentage of that net worth capital required for the travel agents' licence to be used to pay the travel agencies' workers and guides when the travel agencies cease operations?

sections.label: Registration, penalties and licensing guidelines
sections.summary: Asks whether STB could make entities register, and issue guidelines on licensing exemptions given penalties may increase to $25,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Could STB make it compulsory for these entities to register themselves with STB so that we know who they are and what services they are offering?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This will help the authorities in the event where investigations need to be made and tracking needs to be done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Second, since the penalties for unlicensed travel agents may be increased to $25,000, could STB also come up with clear guidelines to educate the public and the players in the sector on when one is exempt from licensing and when one is not, so that members of the public, including our overseas visitors, are clear on the guidelines and will not unwittingly get themselves into trouble?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We need a robust regulatory framework, strong travel agents and capable travel workers and guides to prevail in the future.

sections.label: Protecting guides, consumers and travel hub
sections.summary: Agrees on protecting guides and consumers, keeping a tight rein on offenders, and giving STB more powers to safeguard the travel hub's reputation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I agree with Mr Desmond Choo's emphasis on the vulnerability of guides and the need to do more to protect them, as well as Mr Lim Biow Chuan's plea for us to do more to safeguard the interest of consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We need to keep a tight rein on offenders and a tighter rein on repeat offenders, especially the key appointment holders and directors of travel agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Giving STB more or new powers to impose financial penalties, suspend or revoke a licence is a strong indication that we want to safeguard our reputation as a reliable travel hub.

sections.label: Conciliation service for travel disputes
sections.summary: The speaker suggests STB set up a conciliation service or platform with unions, travel associations, agents and guides to resolve disputes and set standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To this end, I would like to suggest a conciliation service or a platform whereby STB can set it up with the unions, travel associations, agents, guides, to resolve disputes, to discuss matters and to set standards for professionalism.

sections.label: Investing in travel hub status
sections.summary: The speaker says operations have started in Terminal 4 and continued investment, manpower readiness and a stakeholder platform are needed to cement travel hub status.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We have just started operations in Terminal 4.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We will need to continue to invest heavily into future-ready tools, make our travel manpower ready for the challenges ahead and create a platform for stakeholders to resolve disputes and set standards, so as to cement our status as a travel hub.

sections.label: STB power over travel agents
sections.summary: The speaker says the power lets STB protect consumers when travel agents cannot fulfil obligations, but questions its practical use in a MISA Travel-like case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This is an important power which allows STB to step in and ensure consumers are well protected in the event that travel agents are unable or perhaps unwilling to fulfil their contractual obligations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, I wonder if this broad power, as it is currently drafted, will have any practical use in a more likely situation, such as if a repeat case of MISA Travel occurs.

sections.label: Clarification and compensation fund proposal
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the new section helps consumers in MISA Travel-like cases and whether a Travel Industry Compensation Fund will be considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify how this new section will be able to help consumers in cases similar to MISA Travel?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On this note, to complement this new section 28(1)(ga)(i), will the Minister consider establishing a Travel Industry Compensation Fund to provide reimbursements as a last resort to travellers in specific situations, such as insolvency of the travel agents?

sections.label: Online travel platforms as licensees
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether businesses selling travel products on online platforms are caught by the definition of licensees under the Travel Agents Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Travellers are able to purchase travel products on such platforms and, while I appreciate that such businesses have online terms of use, that is merely equivalent to the contracts that traditional travel agents have with travellers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I wish to clarify whether such businesses are caught by the definition of licensees under the Travel Agents Act.

sections.label: Travel agents ceasing operations
sections.summary: Mr Desmond Choo noted in his speech that about 125 travel agents have ceased operations since the beginning of 2017.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Mr Desmond Choo noted in his speech that about 125 travel agents have ceased operations since the beginning of 2017.

sections.label: Sudden business closures 2012 to 2017
sections.summary: From 2012 to 2017 there were 10 sudden closures, about 1.5% of all business cessations in that period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: From 2012 to 2017, there were 10 such sudden closures, making up around 1.5% of all business cessations in that period.

sections.label: Travel agent inaccurate advertisements penalties
sections.summary: Mr Lim Biow Chuan urged action against travel agents publishing inaccurate advertisements, punishable by up to $2,000, while false or misleading advertisements remain a criminal offence punishable by up to $10,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan has urged that travel agents publishing or distributing "inaccurate or erroneous" advertisements be taken to task.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: This will be punishable by a maximum administrative financial penalty of $2,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: For the specific example that Mr Lim has shared, whereby a travel agent advertises "zero-fare tours" but does not disclose to consumers that there will be forced spending on shopping or compulsory tips, such advertisements may be considered "false or misleading", which will remain a criminal offence under the Travel Agents Regulations, punishable with a higher penalty of up to $10,000.

sections.label: STB rejected direct consumer protection measures
sections.summary: STB considered direct consumer protection measures but decided not to implement them as they would raise business costs for all travel agents though only a minority likely cause harm.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: STB has previously considered these direct consumer protection measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: However, we have decided not to implement these measures as it would increase business costs across the board for all travel agents when, in reality, only a minority of our travel agents are likely to cause harm to consumers.

sections.label: Travel insurance insolvency disclosure requirement
sections.summary: Travel agents will be required under the Travel Agents Regulations to inform consumers of their option to purchase travel insurance protecting against travel agent insolvency.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Instead, we will legislate in the Travel Agents Regulations that travel agents are required to inform consumers of their option to purchase travel insurance that protects against travel agent insolvency.

sections.label: Travel agents suspension contractual obligations
sections.summary: Travel agents facing suspension or revocation remain obliged to fulfil existing contractual obligations, failing which they should pass these obligations to other travel agents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan also asked if consumers who had already bought travel packages from a travel agent facing licence suspension or revocation can be allowed to terminate their contract without compensation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: I would first like to reassure Members that travel agents facing suspension and revocation remain obliged to fulfil their existing contractual obligations, failing which they should pass on these obligations to other travel agents to fulfil.

sections.label: No jurisdiction over foreign entities
sections.summary: For foreign entities with no physical presence in Singapore supplying travel products, there are no regulatory mechanisms to act against malpractice due to no extraterritorial jurisdiction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: If the entity in question has no physical presence in Singapore for the supply of travel products, meaning that it is a foreign entity, we do not have regulatory mechanisms to take action against its malpractice as we do not have extraterritorial jurisdiction.

sections.label: Travel Agent Roadmap support
sections.summary: STB and NATAS launched the Travel Agent Roadmap, and STB has supported over 30 projects under the Business Improvement Fund.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Indeed, STB worked with the National Association of Travel Agents Singapore (NATAS) to launch the Travel Agent Roadmap last year, with the aim of enabling our travel agents to become designers of travel experiences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Since the launch of the Roadmap, STB has supported more than 30 projects under the Business Improvement Fund, ranging from the development of technology solutions for better customer engagement, data analytics and the redesigning of business models.

sections.label: Tourist guide refresher course
sections.summary: All tourist guides must complete a Mandatory Refresher Course before renewing their licences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: All tourist guides are required to undergo a Mandatory Refresher Course (MRC) before they can renew their licences.

sections.label: Travel Agents Act amendments
sections.summary: The amendments to the Travel Agents Act and Regulations enhance consumer protection, allow new business models, and keep regulatory cost manageable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The amendments to the Travel Agents Act and Regulations help to improve the travel experience by enhancing consumer protection and creating room for new business models to grow and thrive, while ensuring that regulatory cost remains manageable.
